headline: Meridian Trust Bank moved from 2% to 100% QA coverage and cut compliance escalations by 38%
summary: Meridian Trust Bank's quality team was manually reviewing fewer than 2% of its 410,000 monthly calls, leaving compliance exposure and coaching decisions to chance. With Homayar reviewing every call, the bank reached full QA coverage in eight weeks, reduced compliance escalations by 38%, and gave supervisors a shared, evidence-based view of every conversation.
challenge: Meridian Trust Bank operates retail banking, card services, and collections lines across three contact centers. Its eight QA analysts could sample roughly 800 calls a month against a 42-point scorecard — under 2% of total volume. Regulatory disclosures on fee changes and dispute handling were impossible to verify at scale, and the bank had received two regulator inquiries in the prior year where it could not produce evidence of consistent disclosure language. Coaching was driven by whichever calls happened to be sampled, which agents understandably saw as a lottery. The QA lead described the situation plainly: they were auditing a stadium through a keyhole.
solution: Meridian deployed Homayar against its existing call recording platform with no change to agent workflows. Homayar's speech-to-text pipeline transcribes every call, after which the QA Scoring Agent applies the bank's full 42-point scorecard to 100% of interactions — the same rubric human analysts used, now applied consistently to every call. The Compliance Agent monitors for required disclosure language on fees, disputes, and recorded-line notifications, flagging gaps within minutes rather than weeks. The Coaching Agent surfaces each agent's two highest-impact improvement areas with timestamped call examples, so one-on-ones start from evidence instead of anecdote. QA analysts shifted from sampling to reviewing the flagged exceptions Homayar routes to them — a calibration role rather than a search role.

results.metric: Time to identify a disclosure gap
QA analyst hours reclaimed per month

quote: We stopped guessing which calls mattered. Every conversation is scored the same way, and our analysts now spend their time on judgment calls, not on listening to hold music. When the regulator asked for disclosure evidence this year, we answered in a day.
quoteAuthor: Daniela Reyes, VP of Quality & Compliance, Meridian Trust Bank

seoDescription: How Meridian Trust Bank used Homayar's AI call analysis to reach 100% QA coverage across 410,000 monthly calls, cut compliance escalations 38%, and reclaim 640 QA hours per month.

headline: Northbridge Health Network reduced appointment scheduling errors by 41% and lifted patient satisfaction 9 points
summary: Northbridge Health Network's patient access center handles 180,000 calls a month for scheduling, billing, and referrals — and had no systematic way to find where calls went wrong. Homayar's issue detection identified scheduling-error patterns within the first month, helping the team cut booking errors by 41% and raise patient satisfaction scores by 9 points.
challenge: Northbridge's 14-hospital network centralized its patient access operations, but quality oversight did not scale with it. Scheduling errors — wrong location, wrong provider, missed prep instructions — generated costly downstream rework: no-shows, same-day cancellations, and repeat calls from frustrated patients. The team suspected the errors clustered around specific call types and specialty workflows, but with supervisors reviewing fewer than 50 calls a week, no one could prove it. Patient satisfaction scores for the access center had been flat for six quarters, and clinical departments were escalating complaints about referral handoffs the access team could not trace back to specific conversations.
solution: Northbridge deployed Homayar in its private cloud environment to meet HIPAA requirements, with PHI redaction applied at the transcription layer. The Issue Detection Agent classified every call by intent and outcome, and within four weeks it isolated the two workflows responsible for 63% of scheduling errors: multi-provider referral bookings and imaging appointments with prep instructions. The QA Scoring Agent measured whether prep instructions were actually delivered and confirmed — not just whether the call ended politely. The Insights Agent gave operations leaders a weekly view of error drivers by clinic, call type, and shift, while the Coaching Agent gave team leads specific call moments to review with each scheduler. The access team rewrote two booking workflows based on the evidence and tracked the improvement call by call.
quote: For years we knew errors were happening somewhere in 180,000 monthly calls — we just couldn't see where. Homayar showed us the two workflows causing most of the damage in the first month. Our schedulers weren't the problem. The process was, and now we could finally fix it.
quoteAuthor: Marcus Whitfield, Senior Director of Patient Access, Northbridge Health Network
seoTitle: Northbridge Health: 41% Fewer Scheduling Errors with Homayar | Case Study
seoDescription: How Northbridge Health Network used Homayar's HIPAA-ready AI call analysis to cut appointment scheduling errors 41%, reduce repeat calls 23%, and lift patient satisfaction 9 points.

headline: Velora Telecom cut average handle time 14% and identified churn-risk calls worth $2.1M in saved annual revenue
summary: Velora Telecom's 900-agent support operation was measured almost entirely on speed, with no visibility into why handle times varied threefold across teams. Homayar's analysis found the real drivers — broken troubleshooting flows and unflagged cancellation intent — cutting AHT by 14% while surfacing churn-risk calls that retention teams converted into $2.1M of saved annual recurring revenue.
challenge: Velora's technical support and billing lines handled 1.3 million calls a month across three outsourced sites and one in-house center. Average handle time ranged from 6.2 to 19 minutes for nominally identical issue types, and leadership could not explain the variance. Worse, customers signaling cancellation intent — comparing competitor pricing, asking about contract end dates, mentioning service frustration for the third time — were being handled as routine billing inquiries. By the time churn appeared in the data, the conversations that predicted it were thirty days old and unreviewed. The existing speech analytics tool produced keyword counts that nobody acted on.
solution: Velora connected Homayar to its recording infrastructure across all four sites, giving leadership one consistent measurement layer over in-house and BPO teams alike. The Issue Detection Agent mapped every call to a troubleshooting path and exposed where handle time was actually lost: two outdated modem-provisioning flows accounted for 31% of excess AHT on technical calls. The Insights Agent flagged cancellation-intent signals in real conversation context — not keywords, but patterns like competitor comparisons combined with repeated unresolved issues — and routed a daily churn-risk queue to the retention team. The QA Scoring Agent applied one scorecard across all vendors, ending the calibration disputes that had consumed monthly business reviews. The Coaching Agent identified which agents had mastered the fixed flows so supervisors could spread those techniques deliberately.

results.metric: Saved annual recurring revenue from churn-risk queue

quote: We had been managing handle time with a stopwatch when the problem was the map, not the runner. Homayar showed us the broken flows, and the churn queue paid for the platform several times over in the first two quarters.
quoteAuthor: Priya Raman, Chief Customer Officer, Velora Telecom

headline: Atlas & Shield Insurance shortened claims-call resolution by 22% and cut complaint-to-regulator cases by half
summary: Atlas & Shield's claims contact center was fielding rising complaint volumes with no way to see which conversations were going wrong until customers escalated to regulators. With Homayar scoring every claims call and flagging at-risk interactions the same day, the insurer cut formal regulator complaints by 50% and shortened claims-call resolution by 22%.
challenge: Atlas & Shield handles 240,000 claims-related calls a month across auto, property, and life lines. Claims calls are long, emotionally charged, and procedurally dense — and the company's QA team of six could review only a few hundred per month. Formal complaints to state insurance regulators had risen 19% year over year, and post-mortems consistently found the same pattern: the warning signs were present in calls weeks before escalation, but no one had heard them. First-notice-of-loss calls also showed wide variance in completeness, forcing adjusters to call customers back for missing information and stretching cycle times.
solution: Atlas & Shield deployed Homayar with role-based access aligned to its compliance requirements, keeping claims data within its existing security boundary. The QA Scoring Agent evaluates every claims call against line-specific scorecards, including a completeness check for first-notice-of-loss calls that verifies all required claim details were captured before the call ended. The Issue Detection Agent flags escalation-risk conversations — unresolved status questions, repeated callbacks on the same claim, expressions of intent to file a complaint — and routes them to a supervisor review queue within hours, not weeks. The Insights Agent traced complaint drivers to three specific gaps in status-update communications, which the claims operations team closed with revised callback commitments. The Coaching Agent gave supervisors timestamped examples for each adjuster-facing improvement area, framed around skill development rather than fault-finding — a deliberate choice that drove agent acceptance.

headline: Cardinal & Rowe lifted CSAT 9 points and onboarded 300 seasonal agents to full proficiency 40% faster
summary: Omnichannel retailer Cardinal & Rowe triples its support team every holiday season, and quality historically collapsed with the surge. Using Homayar's coaching and scoring across every call, the company brought seasonal agents to proficiency 40% faster, lifted CSAT 9 points year over year, and turned peak season from a quality risk into its strongest quarter.
challenge: Cardinal & Rowe runs 95 stores and a large e-commerce operation, with a support center that grows from 150 to 450 agents between October and January. Seasonal agents historically took six weeks to reach proficiency — half the season — and supervisors managing 25 new agents each had no realistic way to know who was struggling until CSAT surveys and refund anomalies surfaced weeks later. Order-status, returns, and shipping-exception calls spiked together during peak, and the company's December CSAT routinely dropped 6 to 8 points below its annual average. Leadership had accepted the seasonal quality dip as a cost of doing business.
solution: Cardinal & Rowe deployed Homayar three months before peak season. The QA Scoring Agent evaluates every call from day one of each seasonal agent's tenure, so supervisors see exactly who needs help on which call type by the end of week one rather than week five. The Coaching Agent generates a daily development summary per agent — the two skills to work on next, each backed by real call moments — which team leads use in ten-minute daily huddles. The Issue Detection Agent separated controllable problems from upstream ones, showing that 28% of December contact volume traced to a single carrier's tracking-data delays; the e-commerce team added proactive shipping notifications and removed those calls entirely. The Insights Agent gave the VP of Customer Experience a live view of CSAT drivers throughout peak, replacing the post-season retrospective with same-week course corrections.

results.metric: Contact volume removed via root-cause fixes

quote: Peak season used to be the quarter we apologized for. This year our seasonal hires were coaching-ready in their first week, our December CSAT beat our annual average for the first time, and we deleted a quarter of our call volume by fixing the actual root cause. The data was always in the calls — we just couldn't hear it before.
